name: Localized Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, Nails Only
aliases: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa Localized to Nails

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Localized Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of nail dystrophy including thickening, splitting, and onycholysis limited to fingernails and/or toenails
Skin biopsy showing subepidermal blister formation with scarring limited to nail folds
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the COL7A1 gene associated with dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
Lack of blistering or erosions on other skin areas beyond nails
Positive family history of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa or nail dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of nail dystrophy with histopathological confirmation and COL7A1 mutation detection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of generalized dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and other nail dystrophies.

laboratory: Histopathology demonstrating subepidermal blister with scarring localized to nail folds
other: Negative immunofluorescence mapping for other epidermolysis bullosa subtypes

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of subepidermal blistering on biopsy
Genetic mutations in keratin genes (KRT6, KRT16, KRT17)

redFlags: Development of mucosal erosions or scarring
Signs of secondary infection or systemic involvement
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2022.
Orphanet: Localized dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, nails only. ORPHA:158676.
Uitto J, et al. Molecular genetics of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Matrix Biol. 2017.
